CRITICAL BUG FOUND & FIXED: /app/frontend/app/settings/storage.tsx line 270 called shadow(4) but the helper in /app/frontend/src/theme/tokens.ts only defines levels 1|2|3 → the confirmation modal's shadow map lookup returned undefined and crashed the whole StorageSettings component (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'y')` at tokens.ts:148 shadow -> StorageSettings). Every user opening More > Preferences > Storage & Cleanup would see the app's uncaught error screen. Applied fix: shadow(4) → shadow(3). Screens for Storage/Event/EditProfile could not be re-verified live in a second browser context because the app's auth-restore vs first-fetch race on hard reload of a data screen kicked users back to Welcome (pre-existing web-preview behavior noted in earlier iterations — in-app navigation from Home works fine); the testIDs event-date / start-time-input / end-time-input / edit-birthday / storage-clear-cache / cleanup-media-*/cleanup-history-* are all present in source and route to DateField/TimeField pickers per the code.

rca_of_issue: BUG (frontend, blocking): Storage & Cleanup screen (/settings/storage) crashed the moment it mounted, showing the app's uncaught-error overlay. REPRODUCTION (before fix): log in → More > Preferences > Storage & Cleanup → immediate red-screen 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading y)'. ROOT CAUSE: The destructive-confirm Modal uses `shadow(4)` at /app/frontend/app/settings/storage.tsx:270, but shadow() in /app/frontend/src/theme/tokens.ts:141 only defines the map for levels 1|2|3. The lookup `{1:{},2:{},3:{}}[4]` is `undefined`, and the next line dereferences `m.y` → TypeError. Because the Modal is rendered as a sibling of ScrollView on every render (visible={!!confirm} but the element itself is always mounted), the crash fires as soon as the component mounts, not just when the user opens the modal. FIX: Downgraded to `shadow(3)` (deepest defined level) at line 270. MITIGATION: Also recommend adding `?? map[2]` fallback inside shadow() to make the helper crash-safe for any future out-of-range level.
